cause: CONFIRMED BY CV from the manifest of the same session (2c351168), with the cause named: the overlap is at a CODEC boundary, not a recording gap. Their manifest read: frag 2 = 23:48:57.000→23:49:15.809 (18.809 s), frag 3 = 23:49:11.000→23:49:15.809 (4.809 s, disc=True, boundary="codec") — frag 3 starts 4.809 s before frag 2's declared end and both end at the same instant. The session is hevc_capable, so the hot window is served as HEVC main and the rest as H.264 sub, and the two renditions declare the SAME 4.809 s of wall time. CV's earlier 0.007 s figure came from a GAP-boundary session (boundary="gap"), where spans are genuinely disjoint — they generalised from the wrong boundary type and have owned that. My three fresh gap-free 60 s sessions (.183/.184/.102, 59.850-59.851 s declared, zero overlapping pairs) are consistent: no codec switch, no overlap. So this is a distinct defect from the edge over-serve: CV now tracks D1 = edge over-serve (fix: trim served bytes to the declared span) and D2 = codec-boundary wall overlap (fix: the manifest must not emit overlapping wall spans across a codec switch). Neither is built; sequencing is the operator's
fix: none shipped. CLIENT-SIDE DETECTION IS POSSIBLE TODAY and is the deferred TODO: our fragment rows already carry the boundary type across the C++→QML boundary (PlaybackClient.cpp:436 positional row [cs, ce, wsMs, weMs, disc, boundary, codec, tier, resolution, stream_type]; EvHeroPlayer.qml:880 keeps disc+boundary), so EvHeroPlayer._wallToPos can detect a target that falls inside two fragment spans — and specifically one where the later fragment has boundary=="codec" — and trace it. Detection and trace only at first: which copy holds decodable frames is unmeasured, and a policy chosen on reasoning alone would turn a silent wrong answer into a confident one. Not built tonight because compiling writes object files onto a nearly-full disk. Note our hero already RE-OPENS for a jump that crosses a kept boundary (_crossesBoundary), so the exposure is a seek landing INSIDE the overlapped span, not one crossing it
